title: SubsumptionOps
description: Request/result bodies for the subsumption/* operations (spec.md §8.6). Session-less: pure document-in, document-out, like upgrade/*. The provider shape, the subsumption report, the finding and the policy are design 2.8's documents (its schemas/v1/), carried here as objects; the compatibility report is plan task 7.4's own and is defined below.

contract.description: The consumer side: a Janus contract, or a v1-v4 pact, identified rather than declared (ADR 0011). A pact is converted with design 2.5's rules before the walk; its conversion findings are upgrade/pact's to report, not this operation's.

provider-shape.description: A provider shape (design 2.8 §2), for the same provider the contract names.

report.description: The subsumption report (design 2.8 §6, 'janus-subsumption-report/1'). Every interaction of the contract appears in it, including the ones the provider published nothing for.

format.description: How the consumer document identified itself: 'janus-contract/1', or 'pact/<version>' for a v1-v4 pact converted on the way in.

pairs.description: The (consumer, provider) pairs the host is asking about. The engine never infers a pair from the verification results it was handed: a question nobody asked is not answered, and a pair asked about with nothing attached is answered honestly rather than dropped.

verification.description: Verification run summaries, exactly as the terminal event of a run carries them (spec.md §9.6). Attributed per pair by the summary's own 'consumers'/'providers' members and its 'failures'.

policy.description: Subsumption policy layers (design 2.8 §7.1), least specific first: project configuration, then a per-run override. Scalars override; 'exemptions' accumulate across layers (ADR 0016). A merged document is not accepted in their place, because the merge rule is the part hosts would disagree about.

as-of.description: The date exemption expiry is judged against (RFC 3339 full-date). The engine has no clock, deliberately: it must produce the same answer on every pipe, including wasm32-wasip2. Omitted means expiry is not evaluated, and every applied exemption's date is reported as unevaluated.

format.description: How the consumer document identified itself, as CheckResult reported it.

subsumption.description: This pair's subsumption report, when the host has one. Its absence is not an error: a provider that has published no shape gets replay-only semantics (design 2.8 §6.3), which is what makes the check adoptable per provider.

text.description: The page a person reads: design 2.8 §6.4's finding block per pair, under a decision. Rendered by the engine so that two hosts printing the same decision print the same words.

CompatibilityReport.title: CompatibilityReport
CompatibilityReport.description: The can-i-deploy answer for one run (spec.md §8.6): every pair asked about, why each decided the way it did, and what policy decided it. Owned by plan task 7.4 — design 2.8 §1 lists combining its report with verification results as out of its own scope.

as-of.description: The date exemption expiry was judged against, when the host supplied one.

Decision.title: Decision
Decision.description: 'pass' nothing to say, 'warn' something to read that does not stop the deploy, 'block' stop. Open vocabulary, ordered as written: a host that does not know a value treats it as at least as severe as 'warn'.

PolicyView.title: PolicyView
PolicyView.description: The policy this run resolved to, recorded because design 2.8 §7.1's layering means the answer is in no single file.

exemptions.description: How many exemptions were in force across every layer.

PolicyAction.title: PolicyAction
PolicyAction.description: What a subsumption severity does to the run (design 2.8 §7.1). Both default to 'warn' (ADR 0016).

format.description: How the consumer document identified itself.

reasons.description: One entry per fact, never a summary of several: a pair that said 'block' without saying which of four possible facts blocked it would send its reader back to the raw documents.

findings.description: Every finding this pair's report carried, with what policy did to it. Exempted findings are listed, not dropped: a report that hid them would hide the gap a team accepted.

exemptions.description: What became of each exemption the policy carried.

code.description: Open vocabulary, listed in spec.md §8.6. An unknown code is displayed, never dispatched on: 'action' is what a script reads.

action.description: What this reason does to the decision. 'note' is the third value a Decision does not have: something worth printing that changes nothing.

VerificationView.title: VerificationView
VerificationView.description: What the supplied verification results say about this pair. A missing result is never a pass.

status.description: 'verified', 'failed', 'incomplete' (a run a hook aborted), or 'unknown' — no supplied result covers this pair.

runs.description: How many supplied results covered this pair.

filtered.description: Whether any covering run was filtered: unreplayed variants are not passing ones.

variants.description: The covering run's own variant counts, passed through unchanged — present only when one run covered this pair alone. A run over four contracts reports one set of counts for all four, and splitting them between pairs is not something this document can honestly do.

SubsumptionView.title: SubsumptionView
SubsumptionView.description: What the subsumption report says about this pair, after policy.

verdict.description: The walk's own aggregate verdict, unchanged by policy: an exempted finding is still a 'no'. 'not-checked' means no report was attached.

matched.description: Interactions with a published provider-shape entry (design 2.8 §2.2).

not-published.description: Interactions the provider published nothing for, which were therefore not checked (design 2.8 §6.3).

exempt.description: Results of either severity an exemption silenced.

advisories.description: 'advisory' entries (design 2.8 §5), which no policy governs and no exemption silences.

disposition.description: Whether policy left this finding live or an exemption silenced it.

finding.description: Design 2.8 §4's finding (its schemas/v1/finding.schema.json), carried through untouched.

InteractionId.title: InteractionId
InteractionId.description: An interaction by contract spec §4.2's identity: description plus state names.

ExemptionRef.title: ExemptionRef
ExemptionRef.description: The silencing exemption, quoted where the finding is — the reason a reader is looking for.

ExemptionResult.title: ExemptionResult
ExemptionResult.description: One exemption's outcome, echoing the exemption itself (design 2.8 §7.2's selectors) so a reader of the report does not need the policy file open beside it.

status.description: 'applied' silenced at least one finding, 'unused' matched nothing, 'lapsed' is past its own 'expires' date and silenced nothing.
